studies.description: The Rodent Research-3 (RR-3) mission was sponsored by the pharmaceutical company Eli Lilly and Co. and the Center for the Advancement of Science in Space to study the effectiveness of a potential countermeasure for the loss of muscle and bone mass that occurs during spaceflight. Twenty BALB/c, 12-weeks old female mice (ten controls and ten treated) were flown to the ISS and housed in the Rodent Habitat for 39-42 days. Twenty mice of similar age, and matching sex and strain were used for ground controls housed in identical hardware and matching ISS environmental conditions. Basal controls were housed in standard vivarium cages. Spaceflight, ground controls and basal groups had blood collected, then were euthanized, had one hind limb removed, and finally whole carcasses were stored at -80 C until dissection. All mice in this data set received only the control/sham injection. Brain samples from three flight and three ground control animal groups were cut in half between hemispheres. One hemisphere of each brain was used for generating spatially resolved transcriptional profiling data. Hemispheres were cryosectioned so that 2 consecutive sections from the hippocampus of each brain was placed on Visium Gene Expression arrays. Samples were fixed, stained with Hematoxylin and Eosin and imaged. Imaging was followed by tissue permeabilization to release mRNA molecules from cells for capture onto the array surface. Subsequently, following the 10XGenomics Visium Gene Expression protocol, Spatial Transcriptomics RNA-seq libraries were prepared and sequenced. The other hemisphere of each brain was used for single nuclei RNA-seq and ATAC-seq using the 10X Multiome protocol. In addition, bulk RNA-seq (ribodepleted, target depth of 60 M clusters, PE 150 bp) was performed from a pool of RNA extracted from 10-20 sections from each of 3 flight and 3 ground control samples.

protocols.description: RNA/DNA was extracted using the AllPrep DNA/RNA Mini Kit (Qiagen) following simultaneous purification of genomic DNA and Total RNA from animal Tissues protocol: RLT buffer with 1% beta-mercaptoethanol was added to each tube containing tissue sections. Homogenization was performed using tissue homogenizing beads in FastPrep instrument for 3s. Samples were centrifuged for 3 minutes at RT at maximum speed. The supernatant from each sample was then used to isolate and purify DNA and RNA following the manufacturer protocol. RNA was eluted in 30 ul of RNAse free H2O, and DNA was eluted in 50 ul RNAse free H2O. GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Nucleic Acid Extraction- bulk RNAseq

protocols.description: RNA ribo depletion and library preparation was done with Illumina TruSeq Stranded Total RNA Library Prep Gold (Illumina Inc., San Diego, CA). Input RNA ranged between 46ng and 120ng with RIN greater than 6. Index adapters used were at 1.5 M (IDT, 384-well xGen Dual Index UMI Adapters). 15 cycles PCR were performed. Library fragment size was assessed using Agilent 4200 TapeStation with D1000 DNA ScreenTape (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA) following GeneLab SOP 6.3 Quality analysis of sequencing libraries using 4200 TapeStation System with D1000 reagent kit. Pooled library concentration was measured by Qubit 4 Fluorometer (ThermoFisher Scentific, Waltham, MA) following SOP 4.1-RNA/DNA/miRNA/cDNA Quantification using Qubit Fluorimeter. Library quality assessment was performed on iSeq100 (Illumina, San Diego, CA). GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Library Construction- bulk RNAseq

protocols.description: RNA sequencing was performed by GeneLab Sample Processing Lab on Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Sequencing was set up as following: Read 1: 151bp, Index1: 17bp, Index2: 8bp Read 2: 151bp. PhiX included as control and to increase library diversity. Protocol followed is SOP 7.1-Setting up NovaSeq 6000 and iSeq 100 Sequencers. GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Nucleic Acid Sequencing- bulk RNAseq

protocols.description: UMIs were extracted from fastq files using UMI-tools (version 1.1.2). Raw fastq files from each sample were assessed for % rRNA using HTStream SeqScreener (version 1.3.2) and raw fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.12.1) and MultiQC (version 1.26) was used to generate MultiQC reports.
protocols.name: GeneLab raw data processing protocol- bulk RNAseq

protocols.description: Data were processed as described in GL-DPPD-7101-G (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/master/RNAseq/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7101_Versions/GL-DPPD-7101-G.md), using NF_RCP version 2.1.0 (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_RNASeq_Workflow/tree/NF_RCP_2.1.0). In short, raw fastq files were filtered using Trim Galore! (version 0.6.10) powered by Cutadapt (version 4.2). Trimmed fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.12.1), and MultiQC (version 1.26) was used to generate MultiQC reports. Mus Musculus STAR and RSEM references were built using STAR (version 2.7.11b) and RSEM (version 1.3.3), respectively, Ensembl release 112, genome assembly GRCm39 (Mus_musculus.GRCm39.dna.primary_assembly.fa) and the following gtf annotation file: Mus_musculus.GRCm39.112.gtf. Trimmed reads were aligned to the Mus Musculus STAR reference with STAR (version 2.7.11b) and alignment log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). Aligned reads were assessed for strandedness using RSeQC infer_experiment.py (version 5.0.4), gene body coverage using RSeQC geneBody_coverage.py (version 5.0.4), inner distance was assessed using RSeQC inner_distance.py (version 5.0.4), and distribution of RNA features using RSeQC read_distribution.py (version 5.0.4). Aligned reads from all samples were quantified using RSEM (version 1.3.3), with strandedness set to forward and RSEM count log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). To create a set of rRNA-removed quantification data, Ensembl IDs mapping to ribosomal RNA (rRNA) were removed from the RSEM gene count data. Both the original set of RSEM quantification data and the rRNA-removed data were subject to differential gene expression analysis as follows. A runsheet was generated with dp_tools (version 1.3.8) and the runsheet and quantification data were imported to R (version 4.4.2) with tximport (version 1.34.0) and normalized with DESeq2 (version 1.46.0) median of ratios method. Normalized gene counts were subject to differential expression analysis. Differential expression analysis was performed in R (version 4.4.2) using DESeq2 (version 1.46.0); all groups were compared pairwise using the Wald test and the likelihood ratio test was used to generate the F statistic p-value. Gene annotations were assigned using the custom annotation tables generated in-house as detailed in GL-DPPD-7110-A (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/GL_RefAnnotTable-A_1.1.0/GeneLab_Reference_Annotations/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7110_Versions/GL-DPPD-7110-A/GL-DPPD-7110-A.md), with STRINGdb (version 2.16.4), PANTHER.db (version 1.0.12), and org.Mm.eg.db (version 3.19.1).
protocols.name: GeneLab RNAseq data processing protocol

protocols.description: A cohort of 12-week-old female BALB/c mice were flown to the ISS and housed in the Rodent Habitat and were subjected to microgravity for 39-42 days. Mice of similar age, sex and strain were used for ground controls housed in identical hardware and matching ISS environmental conditions. Mice from the same cohort were dissected at time of launch and used as basal controls. One treatment injection was given prior to launch and the other two treatment injections were given during the mission with around 14 days apart. At the time of injection, Dual-energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA) scan was also performed while the animals were anesthetized by ketamine/xylazine. At the end of the mission, spaceflight and ground controls had blood collected, were euthanized and one hindlimb removed and whole carcasses were stored at -80 C until BSP (Biospecimen Sharing Program) dissection on earth. [Spaceflight and ground control mice- untreated, injected with control Ig-G (sham treated).] The study followed recommendations in the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals and the protocol was approved by the NASA Flight Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
protocols.name: Animal Husbandry

protocols.description: Mouse carcasses were removed from -80 C storage and thawed at room temperature for 15-20 minutes for dissection. Each carcass dissection time was no longer than 1 hour from collection of the first tissue. Multiple tissues, including the heart tissue, were collected from each carcass. Heart tissues were harvested and snap frozen in LN2, then stored in -80 C freezer for sample processing. Brain tissue from spaceflight and ground control groups were shipped on dry ice to SciLifeLab Stockholm, KTH Royal Institute of Technology for processing.
protocols.name: sample collection

protocols.description: Cryosectioning were performed at by SciLifeLab following 10X Genomics Visium protocol. https://www.10xgenomics.com/spatial-transcriptomics/ Visium is a commercially available kit produced by 10x Genomics, which allows to spatially visualize the gene expression of tissue sections. Brain samples from three flight and three ground control animal groups were cut in half between hemispheres. One hemisphere of each brain was intended for generating Spatial Transcriptomics libraries, whereas the other hemispheres will be used for generating single nuclei RNA-seq data. Hemispheres from three flight and one ground control group were cryosectioned, where 2 consecutive sections from hippocampus area of each brain were placed on Visium Gene Expression arrays. Sectioning of brain tissues for bulk-RNAseq was performed simultaneously with sectioning for the Visium spatial gene expression protocol. 10-20 sections from each sample collected from various areas of the brain were placed into eppendorf tubes for RNA/DNA extraction and stored at -80 degrees freezer until processing.
protocols.name: cryosection

protocols.description: The absorbed dose of ionizing radiation received by biological payloads on the International Space Station (ISS) depends on a number of factors, including date and duration of exposure and location of the payload on the ISS. Some of the factors that lead to variations in the absorbed dose rate in orbit are ISS altitude, period during the solar cycle, and location of the sample--ISS module and the specific location within that module. Shielding effects from the biological payload container or habitat have not been taken into account. The measured absorbed dose can vary based on the dosimetry instrument(s) used. Radiation monitoring on the ISS is not standardized across modules; each international partner has its own suite of instruments, with differing technologies, sensitivities and analysis methodologies, including criteria for distinguishing between lightly ionizing particles (mainly protons) and highly ionizing particles (mainly galactic cosmic ray nuclei). Both active and passive dosimeters are used. Active dosimeters are powered and data are read out and stored and/or telemetered to ground. Some active dosimeters provide additional levels of detail such as time resolution, energy deposition and particle identification. Passive dosimeters are unpowered, record constantly and are read out upon return to the ground. The dose in the metadata is the dose recorded by the radiation detector closest to the sample. In most cases that detector will be in the same ISS module; in cases where data from a detector in the same module are not available, the dose is extrapolated using data from periods where data are available from detectors in multiple modules, including the module containing the payload. The duration of the experiment is defined as the time in space during which the specimen was 'living', including the time on the delivery vehicle (e.g. SpaceX Dragon). Once the specimen was frozen or fixed, the experiment was considered stopped. Details of ISS dosimetry and a table with doses for all GeneLab ISS experiment ISS datasets are available at https://genelab.nasa.gov/environmental/radiation.
protocols.name: radiation dosimetry protocol

protocols.description: Sample prep were performed at by SciLifeLab following 10X Genomics Visium protocol. https://www.10xgenomics.com/spatial-transcriptomics/ On the Visium Gene Expression array, the tissue is fixed, stained with Hematoxylin and Eosin and imaged. Imaging step is followed by tissue permeabilization in order to release mRNA from each section. The mRNA molecules are captured by barcoded probes in their spatial location of the array surface. Subsequently, synthesis of cDNA is performed.
protocols.name: Nucleic Acid Extraction- spatial transcriptomics

protocols.description: Sequencing library constructions were performed by SciLifeLab following 10X Genomics Visium protocol. (https://support.10xgenomics.com/spatial-gene-expression)
protocols.name: Library Construction- spatial transcriptomics

protocols.description: The eight libraries prepared from the sources CF1, CF2, CF7 and CG7 are sequenced at the GeneLab Sample Processing Lab on Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Paired end: read 1 at 29 bp and read 2 at 121 bp. PhiX included as control. The 4 libraries prepared from the sources CG8 and CG9 are sequenced at SciLifeLab on Illumina NextSeq500. Paired end: read 1 at 28 bp and read 2 at 150 bp.
protocols.name: Nucleic Acid Sequencing- spatial transcriptomics

protocols.description: The processed data contains the following: Counts data for each brain tissue section including corresponding spot coordinates and images processed by Spaceranger; final object containing the deconvolution results processed using Stereoscope; final analysed objects, corresponding metadata file and final rmarkdown html document showing the final plots from the multiomics analysis; and final analysed seurat object with ST clusters and corresponding annotations. The code for the complete analysis pipeline is provided under the github repository: https://github.com/giacomellolab/NASA_RR3_Brain.

The aggregated counts/fragment files were finally used for the data analysis and are provided along with the raw data. The code for the complete analysis pipeline is provided under the github repository: https://github.com/giacomellolab/NASA_RR3_Brain.
